title: Resolvent analysis of a boundary layer flow over a flat plate
author: Rafael Felipe Terres Queiroz
abstract: This work sets out to use the resolvent formulation to study and understand the linear stability in an incompressible flow, where we assume the system is forced by the non-linear terms in the Navier-Stokes equations. We have developed a comprehensive approach, where we start by laying the foundations of the problem, with some basic governing equations and operators derived from the Navier-Stokes system of equations, highlighting the key considerations for solving a linear stability problem. Then we developed a step-by-step, sort of building-up the tools to approach the final problem. This complete problem consists of a Blasius boundary layer base-flow with one homogeneous and two inhomogeneous directions, where the boundary layer thickness varies along the streamwise component x. We have used Chebyshev discretization for the wall-normal direction y and Fourier in the streamwise direction x. The problem was homogeneous in the spanwise direction z with an wavenumber ?. Two methodologies were used to analyze the stability with the resolvent formulation, i) the more widespread matrix inversion approach, followed by a Singular Value Decomposition and ii) the Arnoldi iteration method, consisting in an eigenvalue algorithm to calculate the optimal gains and forcings / responses of the system. Overall, we found all the results to be very meaningful in a physical sense and in agreement with the literature.
